steps.situation: Files on the shared drive are turning into .locked and a ransom note just appeared on the reception PC.

staff.feedback: Switching off can wipe evidence investigators need. Disconnect from the network first; power off only if you can't (CISA).

staff.text: Unplug the network cable / turn Wi-Fi off; leave the PC on
staff.feedback: Right. Cutting the network stops the spread and keeps the evidence.

staff.text: Keep working, tell IT at lunch
staff.feedback: Every minute online lets it reach more files.

steps.situation: The ransom note lists an 'IT support' number and a payment link.

staff.text: Call the number in the note
staff.feedback: Attackers plant fake helplines. Only use contacts saved in ShieldMate.

staff.text: Call the saved IT contact and tell the owner
staff.feedback: Right. Saved contacts only, and the owner needs to know now.

staff.text: Pay fast to keep the clinic running
staff.feedback: Paying is the owner's decision, never the front desk's, and it doesn't guarantee your files come back.

steps.situation: The shared drive is encrypted. Dr. Rao wants to restore everything from the backup drive plugged into the server.

staff.text: Leave the backup drive alone and tell the owner
staff.feedback: Right. Restoring is the owner's call, and the backup needs checking first.

staff.text: Plug the backup drive into the reception PC and copy files back
staff.feedback: The reception PC may still be infected. It could encrypt the backup too.

owner.feedback: If the backup is old or infected, you restore the problem. Test it first.

owner.text: Test the backup first, then restore onto a cleaned PC
owner.feedback: Right. Run the restore check before trusting the backup.

owner.text: Reinstall Windows and skip the backup
owner.feedback: You'd lose every file since the PC was set up. Test the backup first.

steps.situation: Patient records were on the encrypted drive.

staff.text: Write down what you saw and when, and give it to the owner
staff.feedback: Right. Your notes become the incident timeline.

staff.text: Delete the ransom note so patients don't see it
staff.feedback: That destroys evidence. Leave it and write down what you saw.

owner.feedback: CERT-In expects a report within 6 hours of noticing the incident.

owner.text: Report to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing; start the DPDP breach note
owner.feedback: Right. Report now; the breach note covers the patient records.

owner.text: Don't report: nothing left the building
owner.feedback: Losing access to patient records counts as a personal-data breach under DPDP, even if nothing was copied out.
